admission.justification: Whole-line append with counted stalls is proved by the named passing partial-write cases; single-file member of the family.

applicability: Every tool call through the production boundary.
conditions: One whole line per admitted call on the UTC day, with the whole result filed beside it.
Stalled prefixes and concurrent fragments are counted on the next persisted line without interleaving.
Writes that cannot be admitted are dropped and counted: folder-budget conflict, oversize detail, unwritable location.
exclusions: Processes without a coordination root (tests), which write no log and do not fail.
Reports for the caller to read, which are files of their own, not log lines.
Unadmitted writes (budget conflict, oversize detail, unwritable location), which are dropped and counted rather than persisted.
statement: Every admitted call appends one whole UTC-day line under whole-record exclusion and files its whole result beside it, with secrets omitted and long values shortened; a write that cannot be admitted — folder-budget conflict, oversize detail, unwritable location — is dropped and counted, never failing the call; a stalled prefix never joins the next record and concurrent fragments never interleave.
